title: feat(openclaw-id): member roles come from gateway.roles.definitions

commit.messageHeadline: feat: resolve OpenClaw ID member roles from definitions
fix: order member role activation and fence profile merges
fix(gateway): preserve member authority after main restack
fix(gateway): align member-role callers and CI fixtures
fix(gateway): retain member authority for GitHub publication
test(gateway): seed member roles and recovery ownership in CI fixtures
fix(github): retain historical requester grants on retry

Codex review: blocked before merge. ## What this changes This PR resolves OpenClaw ID member permissions from gateway.roles.definitions and installs editable Operator and Viewer presets. **Example:** An owner changes the operator definition to grant only operator.sessions.read. - **Before:** Operator members retain hardcoded write permissions. - **After:** Operator members receive the configured conversation-read permission. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | The feature has a coherent owner and useful harness coverage, but affected regression fixtures remain invalid and required runtime and upgrade evidence is absent. | | **Proof confidence** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Real behavior proof is not required for maintainer- or bot-authored pull requests. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Feature · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Owners cannot customize OpenClaw ID member permissions because the Gateway hardcodes their role definitions. **Reason:** Maintainer-authored direction establishes the product choice, and the implementation reuses the existing role catalog. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 2 items remain** Keep this maintainer-directed feature open; the role-definition cutover leaves existing HTTP and automation regression fixtures invalid. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `e2b02c186150b9ace2c3adf3ea94ecb29ebfdd25` ## Before merge - [ ] **Update existing member fixtures for definition-based admission (P2)** - Requiring a configured definition also changes existing consumers outside the edited suites. tools-invoke-http.abort.test.ts:381 and the member case in openai-compatible-agent-run.test.ts:128 configure only reader but authenticate an operator member, so their expected successful HTTP requests are now refused. The two OCID cases in server-methods/cron-creator-transports.integration.test.ts likewise configure no operator definition and fail while capturing run authority. Install an explicit operator definition in these fixtures and run all three suites, preserving their existing execution and revocation assertions. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - The review found that existing stored data may not work after upgrade. Show that existing data still loads and works with this change. ## Findings - [P2] Update existing member fixtures for definition-based admission — `src/gateway/openclaw-id/tunnel-principal.ts:200-201` ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: Provide redacted Gateway output exercising member activation and definition edits, plus a latest-stable upgrade preserving existing role settings and data; redact credentials, IPs, phone numbers, and non-public endpoints.
Agent review details ### How this fits together The Gateway maps authenticated OpenClaw ID membership to role definitions, then applies those permissions to connections, HTTP requests, retained work, and session continuations. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Authenticated tunnel peer] --> B[Membership authority] B --> C[Configured role definition] C --> D[Connection and HTTP admission] C --> E[Required access policy] D --> F[Agent and session work] E --> F C --> G[Recovered and scheduled work] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep one configured member-role owner, complete the affected fixture cutover, and preserve existing settings and data through activation and upgrade. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Source inspection establishes that four existing positive regression cases lack the operator definition now required for admission; no target code or tests were executed. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Reusing gateway.roles.definitions is a coherent minimal design, but its existing HTTP and automation consumers must receive valid fixtures together. Full review comments: - [P2] Update existing member fixtures for definition-based admission — `src/gateway/openclaw-id/tunnel-principal.ts:200-201` Requiring a configured definition also changes existing consumers outside the edited suites. tools-invoke-http.abort.test.ts:381 and the member case in openai-compatible-agent-run.test.ts:128 configure only reader but authenticate an operator member, so their expected successful HTTP requests are now refused. The two OCID cases in server-methods/cron-creator-transports.integration.test.ts likewise configure no operator definition and fail while capturing run authority. Install an explicit operator definition in these fixtures and run all three suites, preserving their existing execution and revocation assertions. Confidence: 0.99 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.97 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [bfd85da11eeb](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bfd85da11eebe7a1e35bc0a682c16e61fe5b5652). ### Provenance checked - `Member-role permissions` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (59b8a114bf6dede71999976ddc87fd3edf382c85: Tunnel membership supplied built-in Operator and Viewer ceilings while owner devices retained owner authority.) - `Required access-policy plugins` keeps the original intent (552b54b86c133ad9773cade18b272dd0a081ee67: Role-bound access policies must remain required when their plugin or grant is unavailable.) - `Connection reconciliation` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (a91f7cd52cb399712392ca0ad5b57ac061a68370: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175251 preserved unrelated connections and harmless scope edits; this PR explicitly reconnects members when their editable definition changes.) - `Session-principal continuation` keeps the original intent (d777e01d7e12bd0f69fdfb41925adb24f51b0de2: Profiles without named roles require their recorded authenticated source to resume bounded work.) - `Profile role assignment` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (53dcaaedec195fdaf5af06357557c706d3c0caf5: Named roles attach to durable profiles; this PR explicitly makes membership authoritative for OpenClaw ID member connections.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security None. ### Evidence Acceptance criteria: - pnpm test src/gateway/tools-invoke-http.abort.test.ts src/gateway/openai-compatible-agent-run.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/cron-creator-transports.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 - pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/gateway/tools-invoke-http.abort.test.ts src/gateway/openai-compatible-agent-run.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/cron-creator-transports.integration.test.ts - git diff --check What I checked: - **Pinned introduction and current main:** The introduced diff replaces the built-in member policy table; fetched main still hardcodes Operator and Viewer permissions. ([`src/gateway/openclaw-id/tunnel-principal.ts:197`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e2b02c186150b9ace2c3adf3ea94ecb29ebfdd25/src/gateway/openclaw-id/tunnel-principal.ts#L197), [e2b02c186150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e2b02c186150b9ace2c3adf3ea94ecb29ebfdd25)) - **HTTP fixtures omitted from the cutover:** tools-invoke-http.abort.test.ts and the member case in openai-compatible-agent-run.test.ts publish only a reader definition while expecting an operator member to authenticate successfully. ([`src/gateway/tools-invoke-http.abort.test.ts:381`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e2b02c186150b9ace2c3adf3ea94ecb29ebfdd25/src/gateway/tools-invoke-http.abort.test.ts#L381), [e2b02c186150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e2b02c186150b9ace2c3adf3ea94ecb29ebfdd25)) - **Automation fixtures omitted from the cutover:** The two OCID automation-creation cases capture an operator member under configuration with no role definitions; the changed current-principal check now rejects that source. ([`src/gateway/server-methods/cron-creator-transports.integration.test.ts:195`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e2b02c186150b9ace2c3adf3ea94ecb29ebfdd25/src/gateway/server-methods/cron-creator-transports.integration.test.ts#L195), [e2b02c186150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e2b02c186150b9ace2c3adf3ea94ecb29ebfdd25)) - **Persisted configuration boundary:** Activation writes missing operator and viewer definitions through the canonical config writer, preserving existing definitions, default, and assignments; this changes persisted configuration and requires upgrade compatibility evidence. ([`src/gateway/openclaw-id/member-role-presets.ts:72`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e2b02c186150b9ace2c3adf3ea94ecb29ebfdd25/src/gateway/openclaw-id/member-role-presets.ts#L72), [e2b02c186150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e2b02c186150b9ace2c3adf3ea94ecb29ebfdd25)) - **Full body and discussion:** The complete REST body matches the supplied content identified by sourceRevision c377433ee61da1dad5cde9a709c79529c876548e5a69cf343cc89c03943b3eee. It supplies test results and explicitly excludes live Gateway, relay, and browser E2E execution; comments contain review-status messages only. ([e2b02c186150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e2b02c186150b9ace2c3adf3ea94ecb29ebfdd25)) - **Recorded product tradeoffs:** The supplied maintainer-authorship fact establishes direction; the body explicitly accepts editable administrative scopes, narrower Viewer access, preset installation removing JSON5 comments, and affected-member reconnection after definition edits. Public docs: [`docs/concepts/experimental-features.md`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/experimental-features). ([`docs/concepts/experimental-features.md:273`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/experimental-features), [e2b02c186150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e2b02c186150b9ace2c3adf3ea94ecb29ebfdd25)) Likely related people: - **Josh Lehman:** Raw commit 59b8a114bf6dede71999976ddc87fd3edf382c85 adds src/gateway/openclaw-id/tunnel-principal.ts:3 relative to its recorded parents. ### Preflight source Source unknown. Source comparison at the observed PR snapshot only. Completion is self-reported; body, policy, tests, execution, and report bytes are not verified. ### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Production versus tests** | Production +356/-106; tests +1317/-12 | The growth covers distinct admission, persistence, reload, and recovery boundaries; existing consumer fixtures still need migration. | | **Existing configuration and defaults** | Two presets installed automatically; no new configuration key | Activation persists missing operator/viewer definitions and changes the Viewer preset to operator.sessions.read. | ### Labels Label changes: No label changes. Label justifications: - `P2`: This is a scoped Labs authorization feature with source-reproducible regression-test failures and no demonstrated urgent production incident. - `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`: The maintainer-directed change automatically writes role definitions and deliberately narrows Viewer permissions. - `merge-risk: 🚨 security-boundary`: Owner-authored definitions become authoritative for member privileges, including explicitly configured administrative and pairing scopes. - `rating: 🧂 unranked krab`: Overall readiness is 🧂 unranked krab; proof is 🧂 unranked krab and patch quality is 🦐 gold shrimp. - `status: ⏳ waiting on author`: ClawSweeper has contributor-facing work open and is waiting for author action. ### Rating scale 6/6 🦀 challenger crab · 5/6 🦞 diamond lobster · 4/6 🐚 platinum hermit · 3/6 🦐 gold shrimp · 2/6 🦪 silver shellfish · 1/6 🧂 unranked krab. Overall follows the weaker of proof and patch quality; ✨ marks media proof (a screenshot, video, or linked artifact) that directly shows the changed behavior. ### Workflow ClawSweeper edits this one comment on every review. Live check at `bd9bd69be1657e430d47780643abdddcefcfaa36`: startup with OpenClaw ID off leaves the config unchanged; enabling it writes the expected Operator/Viewer presets without adding a default; the original browser still reconnects using only its device token.

I restarted the isolated Gateway after enabling OpenClaw ID to work around the known hot-enable issue. In the same owner browser, Access was absent and its plugin unloaded before the restart, then visible and active afterward, without a browser reload or another config edit.

Owner, Operator and Viewer connected through the real tunnel. The checks account for implied permissions and call methods that should be denied. Viewer can read conversations but cannot send chat, read logs or list users. Removing Operator's approvals permission closes the existing connection; after reconnect, listing approvals is refused while allowed reads still work. Deleting/restoring Viewer cuts off/restores access. Startup preserves existing definitions and a configured default while adding only the missing Viewer preset. A later restart preserves both members' access and permission boundaries.

A custom role was accepted by the local Gateway and received its configured permissions over the existing tunnel. Staging Discovery rejected publication because it currently permits only Operator/Viewer; restoring Operator recovered publication. That external restriction is not a failure of this PR.

One live check remains incomplete: the test tried to find a member profile by invitation email, but the user-profile list does not expose that email. It failed before calling `users.setRole`, so the member-profile role-mutation refusal was not tested. The other checks continued and passed; this is not full live clearance and does not establish a product defect.

Cleanup is complete: the throwaway claw was retired with all four database counts verified zero, all three test-account sessions were revoked and verified signed out, and the isolated Gateway, processes, port, state, checkout and recovery kit were removed. Nothing was deployed or posted.

Live proof at `8d8aa19b21aa5874c5d882021f77dd4d8931eb21`: all ten original checks passed, along with the separate restart-only Access check, using one isolated staging claw.

Startup with OpenClaw ID off leaves the config unchanged. Enabling it writes the expected Operator/Viewer presets without adding a default, and the original browser reconnects using only its device token. I used the known isolated-Gateway restart workaround after enabling; Access then appeared in the same owner browser without a reload or another config edit.

Owner, Operator and Viewer connected through the real tunnel with the expected allowed and denied methods. Editing Operator's approvals permission closes its live connection and removes that permission on reconnect. Deleting/restoring Viewer cuts off/restores admission. Startup preserves existing role definitions and a configured default while adding only a missing preset; a later restart preserves member access and permission boundaries.

Custom-role publication now succeeds in staging: the snapshot write returned HTTP 204, and authenticated HTTP 200 readback showed `auditor`. The custom-role connection received only its configured permissions. The previously incomplete profile-role check also passed: the test identified the member profile across its join, and `users.setRole` returned “This member's role is managed on the Access page.”

The additional removal check proved that removing a member through Access closes the open connection and makes reconnect fail with `relay_denied (not authorized)`. Re-invitation reached the owner's pending-approval list, but the test helper timed out waiting for a manual sign-in state before it clicked Approve. The reused browser also showed a reset/replaced message. Restored access after approval is therefore not proven; this was not a failed post-approval admission assertion.

Cleanup is complete: the throwaway claw was retired with all four database counts verified zero; all three account sessions were revoked and verified signed out; the isolated processes, port, state, checkout and recovery kit were removed.
